fix.notes: The message text is moved verbatim into the template; deck names containing characters like `<`, `>`, or `&` will now be correctly HTML-escaped by Mustache instead of potentially injected raw. No other uses of the `_safe` pattern were touched.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The `SignUp` view built an HTML string containing `<a>` tags and stored it in `self.signed_up_msg_safe`. The template then rendered it with triple-mustache `{{{signed_up_msg_safe}}}` to bypass Mustache's HTML escaping. This is the `_safe` anti-pattern: it forces raw HTML into Python, prevents the template engine from escaping values, and makes XSS auditing harder.

## What changed

**`decksite/views/signup.py`**: Replace the f-string HTML assignment with four separate plain-data attributes: `self.already_signed_up = True`, `self.deck_url`, `self.deck_name`, and `self.retire_url`.

**`decksite/templates/signup.mustache`**: Replace the `{{#signed_up_msg_safe}}/{{{signed_up_msg_safe}}}` block with a `{{#already_signed_up}}` section that constructs the two links using normal double-mustache (`{{deck_url}}`, `{{deck_name}}`, `{{retire_url}}`), letting Mustache auto-escape values as intended.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing skip, unrelated)

Fixes #12464
